subject.title: Scope memory dreaming sweeps by agent

question: Should OpenClaw accept `plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming.agents` as the durable first per-agent Dreaming scope API, or defer implementation until the broader per-agent Dreaming design is chosen?
rationale: The patch is coherent, but config location, fail-closed semantics, SDK exposure, and schedule/staggering scope are product/API choices that should not be locked in by an unsponsored contributor PR.

options.title: Close Until Sponsored
options.body: Close this PR now and keep the API decision on the canonical per-agent Dreaming issue until a maintainer chooses the shape.

options.title: Sponsor Allowlist Slice
options.body: A maintainer can reopen or request a fresh PR if `dreaming.agents` is accepted as a bounded first increment and schedules are split out.

options.title: Redesign Around Per-Agent Blocks
options.body: Use the canonical issue to design `agents.list[].dreaming`, schedule staggering, or pressure-aware behavior before accepting implementation code.

recommendation.title: Close Until Sponsored
recommendation.body: Close this PR now and keep the API decision on the canonical per-agent Dreaming issue until a maintainer chooses the shape.

likelyOwner.reason: Current resolver/runtime blame and recent Dreaming/gateway history make this the strongest routing signal for the config/API decision.
